input.baseline: Twice a week, about 5 km each. My easy 5 km takes 35–37 minutes. Longest run was 7 km.

asked.question: Do you have a finish time in mind?
Why does it matter?
asked.answer: To finish it with my friends

baselineMeasurements.sourceQuote: Twice a week, about 5 km each.
Twice a week, about 5 km each.

options.rationale: Starting from about 10 km a week and a 7 km longest run, a patient 16-week road adds a third day first, then grows weekly volume and the long run by roughly 10% at a time so you can finish the half marathon with your friends.
assumptions: You keep running 3 days most weeks, with a 4th short day only when it feels easy
Easy runs stay around 7:00–7:24 per km, at talking effort
No time target: success means completing the 21.1 km
Missed weeks are repeated rather than skipped ahead

phases.title: Base: three easy days
phases.progressCheck: Three easy runs a week completed; weekly total about 15 km and long run 8–9 km by week 4

phases.title: Build volume
phases.progressCheck: Weekly total about 20–24 km over 3–4 days; long run reaches 12 km at easy effort

phases.title: Long run build
phases.progressCheck: Long run reaches 16–18 km by week 13 with easy breathing and legs fine the next day

phases.title: Taper and race
phases.progressCheck: Volume eased about 30–40%; you feel fresh and finish the half marathon in week 16

sessions.title: Easy run
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Walk 3 minutes to warm up, then run 4 km at your usual easy pace. You should be able to talk in full sentences. Walk briefly if needed; finishing relaxed matters more than speed.

pace.evidence: Easy 5 km in 35–37 min = 7:00–7:24 per km

targets.progressMeasure: Log time and distance, and rate how easy it felt from 1 to 10

sessions.title: Short easy run
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Your new third day, kept short. Run 3 km gently at conversational pace, staying at the slower end of your easy range. This is about adding a day without adding strain.

pace.evidence: Easy 5 km in 35–37 min = 7:00–7:24 per km

targets.progressMeasure: Note how your legs feel from the Tuesday run before and after

sessions.title: Weekend easy 5 km
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Run your familiar 5 km at easy pace after a 3 minute walk warm-up. Keep it steady and conversational; this is the run that will slowly grow into your long run.

pace.evidence: Easy 5 km in 35–37 min = 7:00–7:24 per km

targets.progressMeasure: Log total time; week total should be 12 km over 3 days

sessions.title: Easy run
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Walk 3 minutes, then 5 km at easy pace. Same feel as last weekend: relaxed breathing, able to chat. If your legs feel heavy, slow to the top of the range.

pace.evidence: Easy 5 km in 35–37 min = 7:00–7:24 per km

targets.progressMeasure: Log time and effort from 1 to 10; aim for 4 or lower

sessions.title: Short easy run
sessions.descriptiveGuide: An easy 3 km to keep the third day going. Stay gentle and conversational; it should feel like you could keep going comfortably at the end.

pace.evidence: Easy 5 km in 35–37 min = 7:00–7:24 per km

targets.progressMeasure: Note any soreness; it should be gone by the next morning

sessions.title: Weekend easy 5 km
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Easy 5 km after a 3 minute walk warm-up. Consider running it with your friends at talking pace. Next week this run starts growing toward 6 km.

pace.evidence: Easy 5 km in 35–37 min = 7:00–7:24 per km

targets.progressMeasure: Week total 13 km over 3 days; log whether it felt as easy as last week

options.rationale: You run 10 km a week now. Four runs a week, growing about 10% weekly, take the long run from 7 km toward 16 km, so you can finish the half marathon with your friends. All runs stay easy, with no speedwork.
assumptions: You can run 4 days a week without pain
Weekly distance can grow about 10% most weeks
The long run can reach about 16 km by weeks 9-10
Missed weeks may mean repeating a week rather than skipping ahead

phases.title: Base: four easy days

phases.title: Build the long run

phases.title: Peak distance
phases.progressCheck: Complete one long run of about 16 km at an easy, talkable effort

phases.title: Taper and race
phases.progressCheck: Weekly distance drops 30-50%, legs feel fresh, and you finish the 21.1 km
